chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from the one who mentioned it, from Dawud al-Sarri, who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'O Dawud! The prohibited [earnings] do not flourish, and if they do flourish, there is no blessing for him in it, and whatever he spends of it he is not rewarded for it, and whatever he leaves behind, it becomes his provision to the Fire.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to prohibited wealth in terms of growth, blessing, and the afterlife?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the metaphysical reality of prohibited wealth, distinguishing between material accumulation and spiritual barakah. He warns that while haram earnings may appear to grow, they lack divine blessing and their consumption yields no reward, ultimately serving as fuel for the Hellfire—a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the purity of sustenance (rizq).
